proof_0481.moves: Both sides unfold to the same search over the slice: matching a character pattern is by definition matching the boolean predicate (· == c), so the proof is definitional unfolding closed by rfl.

proof_0482.moves: The component complement is contained in its image under hom (subset_hom), and an infinite set stays infinite when enlarged, so Set.Infinite.mono finishes it.

proof_0483.moves: Turn the ring homomorphisms into algebra structures via toAlgebra, install the resulting scalar tower (algebraMap of the composite equals the composite of algebraMaps, true by rfl), then invoke the algebra-level statement Algebra.FormallyEtale.of_restrictScalars.

proof_0484.moves: Take an element of s and show it lies in every non-unital subsemiring containing s, i.e. apply the mpr direction of the mem_closure characterization of the closure.

proof_0485.moves: Purely definitional: the plausible-successor relation is literally the inverse image of the iterator's step relation, so rfl closes it.

proof_0486.moves: Rewrite the theory-level biconditional as the conjunction of the two implications (iff_iff_imp_and_imp) and project onto the second conjunct.

proof_0487.moves: Being pairwise with respect to the bottom (always-false) relation says no two distinct elements exist, which is exactly subsingleton; apply the forward direction of pairwise_bot_iff.

proof_0488.moves: Reduce a = top to top <= a via eq_top_iff, then use codisjointness: top <= a sup b, and both a <= a (le_rfl) and b <= a, so top <= a.

proof_0489.moves: Build the instance by checking the isometry condition: the opposite's action unops to the underlying additive action, so the extended distance is preserved by the known left-invariance lemma edist_vadd_left.

proof_0490.moves: Chain the two bridging lemmas through the intermediate model function minEntry?-sub-m: the implementation agrees with it, and it agrees with the list-model minimum on toListModel.

proof_0491.moves: Write the half-open interval as the intersection Iio b inter Ici a, then use that locally closed sets are closed under intersection together with the two known facts that Iio and Ici are locally closed.

proof_0492.moves: Membership in the intermediate field's underlying subfield is the same carrier membership by definition, so the biconditional is Iff.rfl.

proof_0493.moves: Destructure both arrays into their underlying lists, transport array membership to list membership, and apply the corresponding list permutation lemma List.Perm.mem_iff.

proof_0494.moves: Iio is injective on the order, and an injective function turns equality of images into equality of arguments (Function.Injective.eq_iff).

proof_0495.moves: Case-split on the constructor form of the integer argument (ofNat versus negSucc); the nonnegative branches are trivially true and the negSucc branch is exactly the supplied square-inequality hypothesis.

proof_0496.moves: Unwrap the raw tree map to its internal implementation, extract the implementation-level well-formedness from Raw.WF, and apply the corresponding Impl lemma about get! after erase.

proof_0497.moves: Use Filter.hasBasis_self: it suffices that every neighbourhood of the set contains a closed neighbourhood of it, which is exactly the normality lemma exists_mem_nhdsSet_isClosed_subset.

proof_0498.moves: Take the initial segment of the walk up to the given vertex, which is again a path, and compare it with the single-edge path given by the adjacency; in an acyclic graph paths between two vertices are unique (subsingleton), so the two agree and the vertex must be the second one.

proof_0499.moves: Assemble the Equivalence structure from the three already-proved facts that the right-fraction relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive under a right calculus of fractions.

proof_0500.moves: Simp reduces the goal to the rank characterization of membership in the von Neumann hierarchy: a set is contained in vonNeumann of an ordinal exactly when its rank is at most that ordinal, and here the ordinal is the rank itself, so reflexivity closes it.

proof_0501.moves: Rewrite subtraction as adding the negation, then replace the negation by multiplication with minus one, and identify minus one with its UInt8 numeral.

proof_0502.moves: Translate each congruence into divisibility of the difference, then use that a number is divisible by both moduli exactly when it is divisible by their least common multiple.

proof_0503.moves: Induction on the natural number n: the base case is exp 0 = 1, and the step splits (n+1)z as z + nz and uses the addition formula for exp together with the successor law for powers.

proof_0504.moves: Prove both directions: a covering relation gives the weak covering plus distinctness (CovBy.wcovBy, CovBy.ne), and conversely a weak covering between distinct elements is a covering (WCovBy.covBy_of_ne).
